description.en: Learn how Recurrent Neural Networks process sequences by maintaining a hidden state that carries context from past inputs.

story_variants.en:
## RNNs: Networks That Remember

A standard feedforward network sees each input in isolation. A **Recurrent Neural Network (RNN)** has a memory — its **hidden state** — that is updated at each time step and carries information from the past.

### The RNN Equation

At each time step `t`:

```
h_t = tanh(W_h · h_{t-1} + W_x · x_t + b)
```

- `x_t` — current input
- `h_{t-1}` — previous hidden state (the memory)
- `W_h`, `W_x` — weight matrices
- `h_t` — new hidden state

### Implementing a Simple RNN Cell

```python
import numpy as np

def rnn_cell(x_t, h_prev, W_h, W_x, b):
    return np.tanh(W_h @ h_prev + W_x @ x_t + b)

# Process a sequence
h = np.zeros(hidden_size)
for x_t in sequence:
    h = rnn_cell(x_t, h, W_h, W_x, b)
# h now summarises the entire sequence
```

### Sequence Applications

| Task | Input Sequence | Output |
|------|---------------|--------|
| Sentiment analysis | Words in review | Positive/Negative |
| Language modelling | Previous words | Next word |
| Machine translation | Source sentence | Target sentence |
| Time series forecast | Past values | Future value |

### The Vanishing Gradient Problem

> **Key Concept:** In long sequences, gradients must travel back through many time steps. They tend to shrink (vanish) or explode exponentially, making it hard to learn long-range dependencies. LSTM and GRU architectures solve this.

### Unrolling Through Time

An RNN with 5 time steps is equivalent to a 5-layer deep network — but all layers **share the same weights**. This is called **Backpropagation Through Time (BPTT)**.

animation_sequence.code:
import torch
import torch.nn as nn

rnn = nn.RNN(input_size=10, hidden_size=20, batch_first=True)
x = torch.randn(2, 5, 10)  # batch=2, seq=5, features=10
output, h_n = rnn(x)
print(f'Input:  {x.shape}')
print(f'Output: {output.shape}')
print(f'Hidden: {h_n.shape}')

q.en: In an RNN, what is the role of the hidden state h_t?
q.ta: RNN-இல் மறைநிலை (hidden state) h_t-இன் பங்கு என்ன?

en: It stores only the final output label
It holds a fresh copy of the current input x_t
It carries context from earlier inputs to later steps
It is reset to zeros at every time step
ta: தற்போதைய உள்ளீடு x_t-இன் புதிய நகலை வைத்திருக்கிறது
முந்தைய உள்ளீடுகளின் சூழலை அடுத்த படிகளுக்குக் கொண்டு செல்கிறது

b must be added outside np.tanh

b ஆனது np.tanh-க்கு வெளியே கூட்டப்பட வேண்டும்
அணி பெருக்கலுக்கு முன்பே np.tanh பயன்படுத்தப்பட வேண்டும்

q.en: An RNN unrolled over 5 time steps is like a 5-layer network. How are the weights used across those layers?
q.ta: 5 நேரப் படிகளுக்கு விரிக்கப்பட்ட RNN ஒரு 5-அடுக்கு நெட்வொர்க் போன்றது. அந்த அடுக்குகளில் எடைகள் எப்படிப் பயன்படுகின்றன?

en: All layers share the same W_h, W_x and b
Each layer learns its own separate weights
Only the first layer has weights
Weights are re-initialised randomly at each step
ta: எல்லா அடுக்குகளும் அதே W_h, W_x, b-ஐப் பகிர்கின்றன
ஒவ்வொரு படியிலும் எடைகள் சீரற்ற முறையில் மீண்டும் தொடக்கப்படுகின்றன

under_the_hood.summary: An RNN reads a sequence one step at a time and keeps a hidden state: at each step it mixes the new input with the previous state using the same weights, h_t = tanh(W_h h_(t-1) + W_x x_t + b), so earlier inputs echo into later steps.

steps.title: One cell, reused every step
steps.body: The same W_h, W_x and b are applied at every time step, whether the sequence has 5 steps or 500. Unrolled in time the RNN looks like a deep network with shared weights, one copy per step, each passing its hidden state to the next.

stages: output from h_T or every h_t
props.caption: An RNN unrolled over time

steps.title: Worked: a fading memory
steps.body: Scalar RNN with w_h = 0.5, w_x = 1, b = 0 and inputs [1, 0, 0]. h1 = tanh(1) = 0.762. h2 = tanh(0.5 x 0.762) = 0.363. h3 = tanh(0.5 x 0.363) = 0.180. The first input is still present at step 3, but halving each time: this RNN's memory fades quickly.

props.caption: Columns: input x_t, hidden state h_t

steps.title: Shapes in PyTorch
steps.body: nn.RNN(input_size=10, hidden_size=20, batch_first=True) takes input of shape (batch, time, 10). It returns output (batch, time, 20), the hidden state at every step, and h_n (num_layers, batch, 20), the final state. For classifying a whole sequence you usually feed h_n to a linear layer.

steps.title: Backpropagation through time
steps.body: To learn, the loss's gradient flows backwards through every step. Each step multiplies it by w_h and by tanh's slope (at most 1). With w_h = 0.5, ten steps scale it by at most 0.5^10, about 0.001: early inputs barely influence learning. With |w_h| > 1 gradients can instead explode, which gradient clipping limits.

steps.title: Why gated cells followed
steps.body: This vanishing gradient means a plain RNN struggles to connect words more than a few dozen steps apart. LSTM and GRU cells add gates and an additive memory path so gradients survive longer, and transformers later replaced recurrence with attention that links any two positions directly.

under_the_hood.takeaway: An RNN is one small network applied repeatedly with a carried state. That design gives it memory, but also multiplies gradients step after step, which is why plain RNNs forget and gated cells were invented.
